hypothesis: Question: does any between-patient voice->motor_UPDRS signal transfer to unseen patients, or is the train median (dev RMSE 8.379, currently the leader) the best a patient-held-out method can do? Prior evidence: every fitted model measured on development lost to the median (Ridge 8.523, HGB 10.465, idea-1406e7 8.536, between-patient ridge idea-5d99aa 8.467), while idea-5d99aa's authored findings claimed a 28-patient LOPO advantage for between-ridge over median; that claim is unverified against development. idea-82f0cc tried to test this but failed operationally ('private/reflection and I/O attributes unsupported'), which is not a negative measurement, so the H1/H2 question is still open. This analysis (parent idea-82f0cc, rewritten with plain numpy closed-form ridge, dict-key access only, no sklearn objects, no attribute reflection, no printing) uses the development labels legitimately available to analyze() to run leave-one-patient-out over all 35 labelled patients for: train-row median, mean of patient means, between-patient ridge (alpha 1..10000 on log-voice patient means + age + sex), voice-only and age/sex-only ridge, kNN on patient means, and shrunken blends lambda*ridge+(1-lambda)*median; it reports row RMSE, mean per-patient MAE, per-patient win counts vs median, a 300-permutation null for the alpha=1000 ridge LOPO RMSE (patient means permuted, within-patient deviations preserved), the between/within variance decomposition of y, per-feature Spearman correlations of patient-mean features with patient-mean UPDRS, and the exact 28->7 protocol replication with signed per-dev-patient errors. Contrasting outcomes before execution: H1 (near-zero transferable signal) predicts permutation p > ~0.2, all models within noise of the median on 35-patient LOPO, no majority per-patient win, and dev errors spread across patients; H2 (signal exists but shrinkage/level offsets) predicts permutation p < 0.05, a majority per-patient win for ridge or a blend over median with lower LOPO RMSE, and the dev loss concentrated in 1-2 patients with large signed offsets. Decision value for round 7: under H2 with a blend winning LOPO-35 I would submit that shrunken between-patient method; under H1 I would explicitly select the median action b09550c0112a2214dac772c8176445d3932fb70a53d839d2e26bc61dcc2fbca6 rather than spend the last round on another fitted model. Caveats: 35 patients is a small group sample; LOPO-35 partly reuses the development patients that will not be scored, and the interpolated labels mean patient-level noise is not an irreducible floor. Any exception is reported as fallback_used with the message rather than silently returning partial findings.
